P:S ratio by USD = 0.022x (i.e., 46x more selling than buying in dollar terms by named insiders). Asymmetric ratio specifically: Executive Chairman $7.25M SOLD : $0 BOUGHT, CEO $0 : $0, CFO $0 : $0.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: This is the cleanest negative Form-4 setup the framework can flag. Executive Chairman Francescon dumped $7.25M of personally-owned stock 15 days after the Q4 print and ~10 weeks before issuing a guidance CUT on 2026-04-22 (deliveries 9,500-10,500 vs prior 10,000-11,000; revenues $3.5-3.8B vs $3.6-4.1B). Mode-B forensic implication: the most senior insider knew enough about deteriorating order trends (Mar 2026 weakness which Francescon himself flagged in the Q1 press release as having 'intensified even further beginning in early March') to harvest stock at the top of the post-Q4 short-covering bounce, while the COMPANY simultaneously continued to repurchase shares at lower prices with revolver borrowings — a wealth transfer from the public balance sheet to the Executive Chairman. The complete absence of CEO/CFO purchases into a -30% drawdown directly contradicts the 'pent-up demand / 23rd consecutive year of profitability / solid operational results' framing.

rfm_tuples.M_value: Q1 2026 press release (2026-04-22) CFO Dixon: 'Given the impact of the conflict in the Middle East as well as higher gas prices and interest rates on our order activity, we are reducing our full year 2026 home delivery guidance to be in the range of 9,500 to 10,500 homes and our home sales revenues to be in the range of $3.5 billion to $3.8 billion.' Implied cuts: deliveries midpoint 10,500 → 10,000 (-4.8%); revenue midpoint $3.85B → $3.65B (-5.2%). Q1'26 actuals: net new home contracts -11.6% YoY; deliveries -11.9% YoY; ASP -5.7% YoY; adjusted net income $25.6M vs $43.4M = -41% YoY. SG&A ratio 15.8% vs 13.7% Q1'25 = +210 bp deleveraging.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: 84 days between initial 2026 guidance (Jan 28) and the cut (Apr 22). The cut is explicitly blamed on exogenous Middle East / gas / rates factors but Q1 internal orders were -11.6% YoY across ALL five segments (West -14.3%, Mountain -7.8%, Texas -5.2%, Southeast -7.2%, Century Complete -17.5%) which is broader than a fuel-cost shock would explain. The Executive Chairman's sale on Feb 12 (between the initial guidance and the cut) is consistent with information asymmetry on this deterioration. Honest disclosure of the cut, but the timing of the Form 4 in relation to the eventual revision is the load-bearing signal.

By cutoff (2026-05-25) drawdown -30.3% from peak of ~$94 (April 2025) implies cutoff ~$65. Buybacks were therefore executed roughly AT cutoff price, NOT meaningfully above (a positive vs ABG-style destruction). HOWEVER: Executive Chairman Francescon SOLD at $72-73 on 2026-02-12 — i.e., personally exited at materially HIGHER prices than the company was buying back at the same time. Insider Francescon sale price $72.40 weighted avg vs company Q4'25 buyback $59.90 = 21% premium captured by insider. Q1'26 company avg $64.82 vs Francescon sale $72.40 = 12% premium.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: Buyback execution is not the core problem — company prices ($60-65) are close to current trading. The forensic problem is the relative asymmetry: insider out at $72-73, company in at $60-65. The Executive Chairman extracted approximately 18% premium over the company's avg buyback price by selling 100,100 shares directly into the open market. Combined with the revolver-funded nature of the buyback (CCS-05), this constitutes a Mode-B finding the issuer never narrated.

rfm_tuples.R: 10-K: 'In September 2025, we legally extinguished $500.0 million in outstanding principal of our 6.750% Senior Notes due 2027 at a redemption price equal to 100% of the principal amount, plus accrued and unpaid interest' and 'As of December 31, 2025, we had approximately $1.4 billion in outstanding indebtedness... $51.5 million was outstanding [on the $1.0B revolver].'

rfm_tuples.M_value: Refinancing: retired $500M of 6.750% notes (due 2027) and issued $500M of 6.625% notes (due 2033) — saved 12.5 bp on a 6-year extension, basically par-refi. Loss on debt extinguishment of $1.36M (modest). Remaining notes: $497M 3.875% senior notes due Aug 2029. Total notes payable $1,102M. Revolver $1.0B facility with $51.5M drawn at YE25, $203.7M drawn at 3/31/26. Interest paid 2025 $81.3M. The 2029 maturity wall ($497M @ 3.875%) is the operational concern — refinancing at 6.5%+ in 2028-2029 would add ~$13M to annual interest expense (~2.5% of FY25 net income). No near-term (2026/27) maturity wall — actually a favorable maturity profile relative to ABG-style auto-dealer balloons.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: Refinancing is clean and term-extension is positive. Debt mix and maturity ladder are not a near-term distress signal. This is one of the few clearly-passing items for CCS.

Combined with the PP&E declining $85.8M, this is consistent with management quietly exiting Century Living. Not severe — issuer disclosed the revenue/cost lines transparently — but the narrative framing as 'strategic delivery' undersells what is functionally a low-return capital exit.
